players.notes: Amario joined Boro on a season-long loan from Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer of 2026. He was born in Islington, London in May 2005. His football journey began in earnest with youth team Chettle Court Rangers, where he played from the age of eight to 14. The forward signed for Arsenal as an under-15 after impressing on trial. Amario progressed through the ranks at Hale End, and signed his first professional contract in June 2022. He made his first appearance for Arsenal’s pre-season in a friendly against Juventus following the World Cup, in December 2022. Amario was a regular as Arsenal’s Under-18s reached the final of the 2022/23 FA Youth Cup, scoring five goals and assisting three more. He was also Arsenal’s leading goalscorer and assist maker that season in PL2 that season. He left Arsenal for Brighton in the summer of 2024 before being loaned to the Sky Bet Championship with Blackburn Rovers in August of that year. After 22 league appearances and one goal, Amario returned to Brighton in the summer of 2025. He went back to the North West in July 2025, this time joining Bolton Wanderers for the season in League One. Amario, who has been capped up to Under-20s level by England, was instrumental as the Trotters won promotion via the play-offs. He was named League One’s Player and Young Player of the Month in October 2025 and ended the season with nine goals and 10 assists. He played the full 90 minutes as Bolton beat Stockport County 4-1 in the play-off final at Wembley. Amario was a nominee for League One’s Young Player of the Season in 2025/26 and was named in the league’s Team of the Year and PFA Team of the Year. The forward made his senior Brighton debut in August 2026, coming on as a substitute in their UEFA Conference League play-off tie against Tromso. After signing a new contract at Brighton, he now continues his development with a season on loan with Boro.

Sam joined Boro in August 2026 following his departure from Leeds United. He was born in Thurrock, Essex, in September 1993, and moved north as a youngster. The full-back played for York City Schools before joining Leeds United’s Academy in 2005. He signed a scholarship with Leeds at the age of 16 before penning his first professional deal two years later. His first senior involvement came in pre-season ahead of the 2012/13 season, and he impressed so much that he was handed his full debut on the opening day of the campaign. Sam, then working under future Boro manager Neil Warnock, signed a new three-year deal just weeks into that season. Another new contract followed midway through that campaign as Sam continued to catch the eye. He won Leeds’ Player of the Year, Young Player of the Year, Players’ Player of the Year and Supporters’ Club Player of the Year awards. Sam departed for West Ham United in January 2016, where he would spend three-and-a-half years. He made his European debut in the Europa League during that time, and also had a loan spell with Nottingham Forest. The defender moved to Norwich City in July 2019 and had four years with the Carrow Road club. He rejoined Leeds in the summer of 2023 and again became a regular under Daniel Farke. He was a key part of the club’s Sky Bet Championship triumph in 2024/25, providing quality when called upon in both full-back positions. Sam also appeared for Leeds in the Premier League in the 2025/26 season before moving to Boro.

Rokas made the move to Teesside in the summer of 2026. He was born in Stillwater, Oklahoma, in the United States of America in August 2004. He was born to Lithuanian parents and is eligible to represent either country at international level. His parents were both athletes and Rokas quickly showed a talent for sports. He briefly played at Barcelona’s Academy in the USA, after previously representing Sporting Kansas City’s youth academy. Rokas joined Hajduk Split in November 2020 and initially played for the Croatian club’s Under-17s. The midfielder’s professional debut came in April 2022, which is the same year he had a short loan spell with NK Solin. He quickly established himself as a key player with Hajduk, making almost 150 appearances and scoring 27 times. Rokas won the Croatian Cup with Hajduk in 2022/23. He has represented the United States at Under-15, U20 and U23s levels, and played in the U20 World Cup in 2023. In the 2025/26 season, he scored nine goals and assisted four more across 31 Croatian league appearances. Rokas played for Hajduk Split in the 2026/27 season’s European qualifiers, helping the club reach the group phase of a European competition for the first time in 16 years. His contribution was not minor, either. Rokas scored the extra-time winner for Hajduk as they saw off Rakow Czestochowa in the play-off round, a day before making the journey to England. Rokas took a major step in his career by making the move to Teesside.

Ashley was born in Manchester in June 2005. He quickly caught the eye of scouts when playing as a junior with Curzon Ashton, and joined Blackburn Rovers as a 12-year-old. The defender quickly progressed through the ranks at Ewood Park, and appeared regularly for Blackburn’s Under-18s aged 15. He made his U23s debut the following season as he earned his way towards senior recognition. Ashley’s first-team debut came in the Carabao Cup in August 2022, when he became the fourth-youngest player in Blackburn’s history, aged 17 years and 45 days. A Sky Bet Championship debut came four days later, and that was swiftly followed by the signing of his first professional contract. Ashley made his England U17s debut in October 2021 and has since also represented his country at U18, U19, U20 and U21s level, with his first appearance for the latter coming in September 2025. He played 14 times for Blackburn’s senior team in the 2022/23 season, which saw him named the LFE Championship Apprentice of the Season. Ashley’s performances attracted the attention of a number of Premier League clubs, and he joined Tottenham in August 2023. He spent the second half of the 2023/24 campaign on loan with Plymouth Argyle, and was named their Young Player of the Season as he helped them avoid relegation from the Championship. Ashley returned to the second tier in 2024/25 with Stoke City, and made 39 appearances in all competitions. He spent another season on loan at Stoke in 2025/26, this time making 44 appearances as he continued to bolster his development. With more than 100 senior appearances already under his belt, the 21-year-old arrived at the Riverside in August 2026 already full of experience and ready to make his mark on the Championship stage again.

Myles was born in Isleworth, London, in September 2002, and grew up there. He joined Chelsea's Academy aged eight and was initially fielded on the wing or up-front, but was moved to centre-back by Chelsea staff aged 11. He was moved back into midfield three years later, and his versatility remains a strong part of his game. The former England Under-16 international helped Chelsea reach the FA Youth Cup final in 2019 and then scored seven goals in 13 Premier League 2 appearances in 2020/21. Myles joined Brentford for an undisclosed fee and in his first season with the Bees, he made first-team appearances in two cup matches, and was part of the B team’s 2021/22 London Senior Cup-winning squad. Myles joined Forest Green Rovers on loan for the 2022/23 season, and even captained the team on multiple occasions across 40 Sky Bet League One appearances. He made his Premier League debut against Luton Town in December 2023, helping Brentford to a 3-1 win. It was one of five appearances he made that season for the Bees. A loan to Portsmouth followed in January 2024, where Myles helped the club to the League One title. Myles stepped up to Championship level the following season, playing 30 times in a loan spell with Swansea City. He made his final Brentford appearance in a 4-2 win at Everton in January 2026, and then moved to Oxford United on a short-term deal. After 20 appearances with Oxford, he left the club following the expiry of his contract at the end of the 2025/26 season and joined Boro.

Radek was born in the Czech town of Vsetin in October 2003. His first club was Sigma Olomouc in his homeland, where he progressed through the junior ranks. The 6ft 6in goalkeeper’s form attracted attention across Europe, including England, where he moved to Manchester United in 2020. He quickly made an impact in Manchester, and by the 2021/22 season he was first choice for the Red Devils’ Under-18s, helping them win the FA Youth Cup and reach the quarter-finals of the UEFA Youth League. Radek progressed into Man United’s U21s and made his first appearance for the senior team in pre-season ahead of the 2023/24 season. He made his senior debut while on loan with Accrington Stanley later that campaign, making 18 appearances in League Two. After another pre-season with Man United’s first-team squad, Radek joined Austrian Bundesliga side Blau-Weiß Linz on loan for 2024/25. He kept a clean sheet on his debut and established himself as first-choice, making 26 league appearances. Another loan spell followed in 2025/26 as Radek made the move to Bristol City. It was a successful stint at Ashton Gate, with Radek being named the club’s Player of the Year and Players’ Player of the Year. He was nicknamed ‘The Wall’ by supporters and made 41 appearances for the Robins. Radek has been capped by Czech Republic at U15, U17, U19 and U20 level, and departed Man United on a permanent basis in August 2026 to continue his football journey at Boro.

Kyle was born in Chipping Barnet in September 2001 and joined Wigan Athletic’s Academy at the age of 13. The forward signed his first professional contract for the Tics in February 2019 and made his senior debut in October 2021. While there, he represented Scotland’s youth teams from Under-18 to U21 level. He scored his first goal for Wigan in December 2020 in a 1-0 win over Sunderland in Sky Bet League One. In the same month, Kyle scored his first senior hat-trick as Wigan defeated Burton Albion 4-3. The 2021/22 campaign saw the forward join Swansea City, but after making just two appearances for the Swans, he moved to League One Cheltenham Town on a season-long loan to gain more EFL experience. Kyle scored four goals before being recalled in January 2022, and the second half of the season saw him make 10 substitute appearances for Swansea. Another loan was on the cards for the 2022/23 season as Kyle joined Oxford United, where he scored 10 times in 41 appearances. His impressive form at the U’s earned him a permanent move to Blackpool. Kyle spent two years at Blackpool where he made 66 appearances, scoring nine times including a goal in the Emirates FA Cup against Nottingham Forest. In January 2025, Kyle made the move to Hull City. In his first full season with the club, he helped the Tigers get promoted to the Premier League, before he joined Boro in the summer of 2026.

Will was born in Welwyn Garden City in April 2005 before being raised in St Albans. The striker was initially in Arsenal’s Academy and joined Sheffield United in January 2021. It was in Yorkshire that he started to shine, with the 2021/22 campaign seeing scouts across the country take notice of his talents. Will captained the Blades’ Under-18s as they won the Professional Development League national title in an unbeaten season. He was the league’s top scorer. He scored 38 goals in 48 age group appearances for the Sheffield club during his time there. Spurs won the race for his signature in August 2022, and he scored twice on his debut for their U18s, before notching his first hat-trick two months later. The 2023/24 season was another big success for Will as he was named the Premier League 2 Player of the Season. He was Spurs’ top scorer, with 23, as they won the title. Will’s progress was rewarded with a senior debut in October 2024 as he started Spurs’ Europa League match against Ferencvaros. His first goal came in the same competition a month later, against Galatasaray, and another month followed before he made his Premier League debut. Will’s first taste of the Sky Bet Championship came in the second half of the 2024/25 season, when he made 11 appearances for West Bromwich Albion. He then joined Oxford United on loan for the entirety of 2025/26. Although Oxford were relegated, it was a season of huge strides forward for Will, who scored 11 times in the Championship. That saw him win Oxford’s Golden Boot, and he was also named their Young Player of the Year. With one-and-a-half years of Championship experience under his belt, Will made the move to Boro from Spurs in July 2026.

Sebastian was born in London before being raised in Columbus. The midfielder played for Hammarby's youth team between 2012 and 2013 while his father, Gregg Berhalter, managed the club. However, in 2014 he joined Columbus Crew, where he climbed through the Academy ranks. Sebastian was announced as a Homegrown Player in 2020 and got his first taste of MLS football against FC Cincinnati. It was a successful first season for the midfielder, who made nine appearances and helped his side lift the MLS Cup. The following season saw Sebastian join Austin FC on loan. He made his debut for the MLS side in a 3-1 victory over the Colorado Rapids and went on to make 18 appearances during the season. Sebastian was traded to Vancouver Whitecaps FC in February 2022 and made 18 appearances in his first season. The following campaign, he took another step forward in his development by scoring his first MLS goal in a 6-2 win over Houston. The 2023 season also saw the Whitecaps win the Canadian Championship for the second consecutive year. Sebastian made it three Canadian Championships in a row in 2024, while also registering two goals and four assists in MLS as the Whitecaps reached the MLS Cup play-offs. The 2025 season was a standout campaign for Sebastian, as he scored four goals and provided 10 assists. Vancouver reached the MLS Cup final but were beaten 3-1 by Inter Miami. This season, Sebastian has scored six goals and provided four assists in 14 MLS appearances. On the international stage, he made his debut for the United States at the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup. His first goal for the USMNT came in a 5-1 win over Uruguay, a match in which he also recorded an assist. After impressing for Vancouver, Mauricio Pochettino selected him as part of his 26-man squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The midfielder featured in every game for the USMNT during the tournament on home soil, scoring and assisting in their final group stage match against Turkey. With plenty of experience under his belt, the 25-year-old now makes the move to Teesside.

Max was born in the city of Fresno, California, in April 2001. After starting playing football aged five, he spent much of his youth days with California Odyssey Soccer Club, where he spent nine years. He attended San Joaquin Memorial High School, where he was named the league’s MVP for two years in a row.  At that stage, Max played as a forward, and his final season with that team saw him score 50 goals and provide 20 assists . He attended the University California, Davis, after being offered a full-ride scholarship as a junior. He led his team to a Big West Championship in his first year and was named the Big West’s Offensive Player of the Year in his second, despite missing five months with a broken foot. Max decided to leave college and play professionally ahead of the 2022 season, when he signed a contract with MLS Next Pro side San Jose Earthquakes II. After one season there, he was included in the 2023 MLS SuperDraft, and became the first player to be drafted out of MLS NEXT Pro when he was selected by Columbus Crew. Max excelled as a wing-back across two-and-a-half seasons with the Crew, winning the MLS Cup in 2023 and Leagues Cup in 2024. He was called up by the USA senior squad for the first time in January 2025 and made his debut against Venezuela. He was a regular for his country in the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup as the Americans finished as runners-up. Max has since gone on to appear more than 20 times for his country, including at the 2026 World Cup on home soil, as the USA reached the last 16. He was selected to play for MLS All-Stars in the 2025 and 2026 MLS All-Star Games before making the move to Boro in August 2026.

Jeremy was born in the Spanish capital, Madrid, in June 2002. His parents are Ecuadorian, and they moved as a family to England when Jeremy was aged seven. He was picked up as a youngster by Charlton Athletic, where he stayed for eight years. While there, he was called up by England at Under-16 level, and attracted the attention of Portuguese giants Benfica. Jeremy moved there in 2018 and continued his rise through the England ranks, representing the Three Lions’ U17s and U18s. The wideman had been tracked by Brighton during his Charlton days and they kept tabs on him at Benfica, too, before signing him in 2021. His professional debut was just around the corner, with Jeremy replacing future World Cup winner Alexis Mac Allister in an EFL Cup win over Swansea City in September 2021. It was around this time that he decided to declare for Ecuador internationally, and he made his debut for the country against Bolivia in October 2021. Jeremy made his Premier League debut against Leeds United a month later and signed a new contract in January 2022. He was named Brighton’s Young Player of the Season for 2021/22 and was then called up by Ecuador for the World Cup in Qatar. He went on to play a part in all three of their group games. The 2022/23 campaign was a more frustrating one, but he did register his first Premier League assist and played another nine times in the competition. A loan was deemed essential to his development, and he had two in 2023/24, playing 20 times for West Bromwich Albion and 20 times for Ipswich Town in the Sky Bet Championship. He scored twice for the Baggies – including his first professional goal, against Boro – and three times for the Tractor Boys. That included a crucial, last-gasp winner against promotion rivals Southampton as Ipswich went on to claim a place in the Premier League. Jeremy was back in the Championship for 2024/25, adding another promotion to his CV with Burnley, appearing 35 times. He appeared in the 2024 Copa America and has represented his country 27 times. The 2025/26 season saw Jeremy loaned out to Cremonese in Italy’s Serie A, with Leicester City legend Jamie Vardy among his team-mates. He was unable to force his way into a starting role before being recalled by Brighton, and joined Boro in January 2026, initially on a loan arrangement which became permanent.

Fin was born in Kingston upon Thames and is a product of Chelsea’s Academy, having joined the London club at an early age. He demonstrated his versatility while with Chelsea, mainly playing as a centre-back but also performing well at left-back and in holding midfield. Fin's departure from Chelsea at the age of 16 prompted a move to Aston Villa, where he developed into an eye-catching, ball-playing full-back, but also continued to excel in other positions, too. He signed his first professional contract with Villa in July 2022, with another deal following in April 2024. By that time, he had firmly established himself with the club. He was a regular in the U18 Premier League in 2021/22, also playing six times for the U21s in PL2. He had seven goal involvements in 17 appearances in all competitions the following season, before 2023/24 saw him become a mainstay in PL2. Fin was now also beginning to make his mark at first-team level. He was an unused substitute against former club Chelsea in the Emirates FA Cup in January 2024, and his debut came four months later, when he was brought on against Olympiacos in the semi-final of the UEFA Europa Conference League. Fin made his first appearance in the Premier League in May 2024, coming on as a substitute away to Crystal Palace. The left-sider – who is a cousin of Arsenal and England midfielder Declan Rice – signed for Spanish club Real Union on a season-long loan in August 2024. The move saw him play regularly in the third-flight of Spanish football, making 27 appearances. Fin moved on loan to Swindon Town in League Two in July 2025, and went on to have an outstanding first half of the season. Swindon occupy a promotion position just beyond the midway point, with Finley’s appearances playing a key part in that. He played 23 times for the Robins in the league, scoring twice and assisting seven more goals, while he also registered two assists in the EFL Trophy. His appearances were mainly at left-back and on the left of midfield. He made the move to Boro in January 2026.

Leo was born in Kingston upon Thames in August 2005. He joined the ranks of boyhood club Chelsea aged just five before leaving for Wimbledon two years later. His dad, Stewart, played for Wimbledon between 1991 and 2000, and also represented Wycombe Wanderers. Leo was with Wimbledon from the age of seven to 14, and was the youngest player to ever represent the club’s Under-18s side. During his time at Wimbledon, Leo progressed from a defensive role to his current position in attacking midfield. He moved back to Chelsea in 2020 and went on to captain the club at Under-18s and U21s levels. Leo signed his first professional deal at Chelsea in the summer of 2022 as he continued his rapid progress. He played a starring role in a PL2 game against Boro’s U21s in February 2024, coming on as a second-half substitute before registering a goal and two assists in a 3-1 win for Chelsea. That was a month after he made his senior debut, which ironically was also against Boro. He came on for the final five minutes in the second leg of the Carabao Cup semi-final. He bolstered his first-team experience the following season on loan with Shrewsbury Town in League One, where he scored twice in 24 appearances. Leo – who has represented England at every level from U15s to U19s – signed on loan for Huddersfield Town, again in League One, in the summer of 2025. The first half of the season was a huge success for the midfielder, who scored 10 goals in 23 league appearances for the Terriers. He was then recalled by Chelsea before joining Boro on a permanent deal in January 2026, making 11 appearances in his first half-season.
